_comment: Which books exist and how they are built from the pools in tools/library/. See tools/build_books.mjs. One book per (number of shapes, board size); each runs through every difficulty tier, easiest first. A puzzle is in at most one book.
_sparseShare: Within each shape and tier a book only draws from the sparsest share of the puzzles (fewest blocked cells), as far as that leaves enough: the original L-panel puzzles have few black squares, and a book that takes puzzles by difficulty alone is mostly dense.
_tierWeights: Share of a book each tier gets (1 unless listed). Read as counts for a 400-puzzle book: 40 Beginner, 180 Medium, 130 Hard, 50 Expert (Beginner is the least interesting tier, so it is small; Expert is the puzzles the hint rules cannot finish, the same share in every book). A tier with too few puzzles gives up what it cannot fill, the others sharing the difference.
_minBoardDistance: A book keeps only one of a family of siblings: puzzles with the same tile spec whose blocked cells differ in at most this share of the board (0.08 = 5 cells on 8x8), after any rotation or reflection. Short books are topped up with other puzzles.
_sharedTileShare: The other sibling test, by board size: two puzzles with the same tile spec are siblings when at least this share of their tiles sit in exactly the same cells (after any rotation or reflection of the board). Higher on small boards, where a few tiles repeat by chance. Two Beginner puzzles are never siblings by this test.
_groupKeys: A group may override tierWeights, and may set tierMaxBlocked: a looser blocked-cell cap for some tiers (the Beginner and Expert puzzles of the sparse books need more blocked cells than the 17% the rest use, so every book can have the same share of each tier).
_maxLineShare: A tier holds at most this fraction of its puzzles in line-piece puzzles (domino, I tromino, I tetromino, I pentomino; pairs of only those). On sparse boards they are almost the only shapes with Beginner puzzles, so a book's opening was mostly them. The tier gets a little smaller instead of refilling. Like shapeWeights, published puzzles are only dropped with --trim.
_shapeWeights: Relative share of a book each shape (or pair) gets within a tier; unlisted shapes weigh 1. The 'boring' shapes weigh a third: they can only make Beginner or Medium puzzles that all use the same single technique (the line pieces domino, I tromino, I tetromino and I pentomino, and the rigid pentominoes T, U, V, Z and X). A rebuild only adds puzzles unless run with --trim, so new weights take full effect with --trim.
_shapeBoost: Multiplies the weight of every puzzle whose tile spec contains the shape (a single shape or a pair with it), on top of shapeWeights: the L tetromino is a favourite, so it gets twice the share of an ordinary shape.

_secondary: A group with secondary: true is listed under "More books" in the book picker; the first two groups (sparse boards, at most 17% blocked) are the main books.
